 Judgment

The claimants, who are the parents of the deceased Vinodkumar Nagendra Balikai are before this Court in this appeal not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded under the judgment and award dated 04.07.2016 passed in MVC No.254/2012 on the file of the Member,
M.A.C.T.-II, Bagalkot (for short, 'Tribunal') and praying for enhancement of compensation.

2. Brief facts of the case are that, the appellants/claimants, who are the parents of the deceased Vinodkumar Nagendra Balikai, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of Vinodkumar Balikai that took place on 15.08.2011 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-02/AH-7755.
It is submitted that the deceased was aged 24 years as on the date of the accident and had completed Bachelor in Engineering degree.
It is stated that the deceased was expected to get good job on the basis of his BE degree.
On issuance of notice, respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their learned counsel.

Respondent No.1 filed written statement stating that the vehicle was insured with respondent No.2-Insurance Company and the rider of the motorcycle was having valid driving licence as on the date of the accident.

Respondent No.2-Insurance Company in its objection contended that the rider of the motorcycle was not having valid driving licence and accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.

4. Before the Tribunal, to prove their case, father of the deceased himself examined as PW1 and one Kishor Rajanna G. was examined as PW2 apart from marking the documents as Exs.P1 to P40;
whereas the respondents examined RW1 and marked 5 documents as Exs.R1 to R5.

The Tribunal based on the material on record allowed the claim petition in part and awarded a total compensation of Rs.22,08,808/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization under the following heads:

5. While awarding compensation, the Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month, adopted multiplier of 18, deducted 50% towards the personal expenses of the deceased since he was a bachelor, but failed to award compensation under the head of future prospects.
Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation, the claimants are before this Court in this appeal praying for enhancement of compensation awarded.

6. Heard the learned counsel Sri.D.V.Pattar for the appellants, learned counsel Sri.Nagaraj C.Kolloori for respondent No.2-Insurance Company and perused the appeal papers along with original records.
7.
Sri.D.V.Pattar, learned counsel appearing for appellants-claimants would submit that the deceased had good future having acquired BE qualification.
He submits that PW2 who studied along with the deceased is drawing a salary of more than Rs.40,000/- per month on acquiring BE degree.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month which is on the lower side and prays for modifying the same on the higher side.

Further, learned counsel would submit that the Tribunal has failed to NC: 2024:KHC-D:7803-DB award compensation under the head of future prospects which the claimants are entitled at 40% of the assessed income of the deceased since the deceased was 24 years at the time of the accident.

Further, learned counsel would submit that the Tribunal failed to award consortium in terms of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs.
Nanu Ram and Others1.

8. Per contra, Sri.Nagaraj C.Kolloori, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company would submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just compensation and it needs no interference.
Learned counsel further submits that the notional income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.20,000/- per month is proper and correct.
He submits that no material is placed on record to reassess the income of the deceased.
Further, learned counsel would submit that PW2 has not studied with the deceased and salary drawn by him cannot be basis to determine the income of the deceased.

Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text:
Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers along with original records, the following point would arise for our consideration:
Whether the claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation?

The above point is answered partly in the affirmative for the following reasons:
10.
The accident that took place on 15.08.2011 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-02/AH-7755, resultant death of Vinodkumar Nagendra Balikai is not in dispute in this appeal.
The claimants are in appeal praying for enhancement of compensation.
Moreover, the respondent No.2-Insurance Company has not filed appeal, it has satisfied the award.
11. Ex.P14 is a certificate of degree in Bachelor of Engineering in respect of deceased Vinodkumar Balikai.
The deceased completed his Bachelor degree in Engineering in the year 2010.
PW2 is stated to have studied along with the deceased and in terms of Ex.P37 PW2-Sri.Kishor Rajanna G., is receiving salary of Rs.42,475/- per month.

Learned counsel for appellants-claimants prays for assessing the income of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7803-DB deceased atleast at Rs.40,000/- per month taking note of Ex.P37.
12.
We have gone through Ex.P37 and the degree certificate of the deceased.
No doubt, the deceased was possessing Bachelor of Engineering degree, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month.
The person having Bachelor of Engineering degree, a technical qualification, would have earned more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
In that light of the matter, the income of the deceased is reassessed at Rs.25,000/- per month as against Rs.20,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.
13. The deceased was aged 24 years as on the date of the accident.

In terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others2 the claimants would be entitled to compensation under the head of future prospects at the rate of 40% of the assessed income.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the claimants would be entitled for adding 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
The multiplier adopted by the Tribunal at 18 and deduction at 50% of the assessed income of the deceased since he was bachelor, is proper and correct.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for a modified compensation on the head of loss of dependency as under:
Rs.25,000 + 40%(future prospects) X 12(months) x 18(multiplier) x 50%(deduction)
= Rs.37,80,000/-
15.

In terms of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. referred to supra, the claimants would be entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/- each apart from Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

2. Loss of estate & Funeral 30,000/-

19. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal is allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment & award of Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.39,18,818/- as against Rs.22,08,818/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization.

d) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company shall deposit enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7803-DB within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In that light of the matter, the income of the deceased is reassessed at Rs.25,000/- per month as against Rs.20,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.
13. The deceased was aged 24 years as on the date of the accident.
Accordingly, the claimants would be entitled for adding 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
The multiplier adopted by the Tribunal at 18 and deduction at 50% of the assessed income of the deceased since he was bachelor, is proper and correct.
Thus, the claimants would be entitled for a modified compensation on the head of loss of dependency as under:
Rs.25,000 + 40%(future prospects) X 12(months) x 18(multiplier) x 50%(deduction)
= Rs.37,80,000/-
15.

Insofar as award of compensation by the Tribunal under the head of medical expenses is concerned, the same is unaltered.
